title: Explicit finite evaluation of a quotient-tower complex
statement: For a small site J, commutative ring A, ideal I and integer n ≥ 0, applying quotient-tower reduction to a cochain complex and then evaluating at n is naturally isomorphic to finite quotient scalar extension followed by scalar restriction. The endpoints are the iterated complex functors, and the comparison is the identity in every degree.

proof.text: The ordinary evaluated quotient tower is definitionally scalar extension to A/I^(n+1) followed by restriction. Use its identity natural isomorphism and the explicit complex-square construction. The hom formula for that construction reduces every degree to the ordinary identity. Thus the equality includes all ideals, the zero ring and n = 0 without any cancellation or flatness hypothesis. Extensionality of chain maps then proves the full identity-chain-map formula quotientEvaluationComplexIso_hom_id.

lean.statement:
def quotientEvaluationComplexIso :
    (reductionTower J A I false).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        ((evaluation ℕᵒᵖ (Mod (constant J A))).obj (op n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ≅
      (change (quotient J A I n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙
        (res (quotient J A I n)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
